content.text:
I've submitted index 91 (Ca 0.21, Cu 0.36, V 0.43). It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.67%, but I can't say it's the best composition in the library: I measured only 3 of the 158.

With just 3 merit measurements, I kept calcium fixed at about 0.21 and changed the copper-to-vanadium ratio:

| Index | Cu | V | EQE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 139 | 0.54 | 0.24 | 0.47% |
| **91** | **0.36** | **0.43** | **0.67%** |
| 69 | 0.26 | 0.52 | 0.38% |

EQE peaked near a 1:1 copper-to-vanadium ratio along this line. From what I know of these materials, copper vanadates at that ratio are active photoanodes under 455 nm (2.72 eV) light. The calcium-rich and vanadium-rich corners weren't measured; I skipped them because calcium vanadates probably absorb little light at this energy. Other calcium levels near this copper-to-vanadium ratio weren't tested either, so a better composition could be there. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, because peak positions alone wouldn't have told me where to spend the merit measurements.
